💡 Economic Reality: High price gaps (e.g. 29.8x for Black Pepper or 8.8x for Dry Chillies) stem from local harvesting gluts vs metro consumption hubs. Agricultural logistics companies generate substantial profits by arbitraging between these mandis.
1. Quality & Moisture Discrepancy

Crops like Arecanut and Jeera are graded into unpolished, semi-dry, and export quality, leading to large legitimate spreads within the same APMC auction hall.

2. Horticultural Spoilage

Tomatoes and leafy vegetables perish rapidly without refrigeration. Evening liquidation prices frequently plunge by 50% below morning peak rates.

3. Transit Overhead & Geography

Mandis in the North East or Jammu & Kashmir have higher freight costs and limited transport logistics, driving significant localized price premiums.
